name: UH-1 Huey / Bell 205 / 212
variants: UH-1B and other ex-military civil examples
summary: The classic two-blade utility helicopter: ex-military UH-1H and civil Bell 205/212s still fight fires and lift cargo across the US, and the USAF flies twin-engine UH-1Ns and TH-1Hs.

wings: Two-blade teetering main rotor on a tall mast
Single-engine versions often show a stabilizer bar across the mast below the blades
engines: UH-1H/205: one engine on the roof with a single exhaust pipe angled up behind the cowling
UH-1N/212: a 'Twin-Pac' with two exhausts side by side and a wider rear cowling
fuselage: Boxy cabin with large sliding doors and a rounded nose with chin windows
Sloping windshield with an overhead greenhouse panel
tail: Two-blade tail rotor at the top of the fin
Small synchronized elevators (horizontal stabilizers) mid-way along the tail boom

tellTales: Two-blade main rotor over a boxy sliding-door cabin on skids
Two-blade tail rotor at the top of a short fin
Small stabilizers halfway along a long tapering tail boom

confusedWith.howToTell: The 412 has the same airframe but a four-blade main rotor; the Huey family has two blades.
The UH-1Y has four-blade main and tail rotors and a FLIR nose; the older Hueys have two-blade main and tail rotors.
The JetRanger is far smaller with a teardrop cabin and no big sliding door; the Huey is a large boxy utility helicopter.
The Bell 214B has wide-chord blades with no stabilizer bar and one large exhaust duct; the Huey has a stabilizer bar above the head and a slimmer body.

usCount.source: FAA registry: ~560 civil UH-1/204/205/212 + USAF ~61 UH-1N and 28 TH-1H (Air & Space Forces 2026)
